items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: But it seems as though Charlie Johnson would usually go down there in the summer but we got the job.

ctx.x: Musical. I'd ask him various questions of this. And he said, I've lived in Europe, I've lived in (inaudible). He'd explain it to me. And then if I wouldn't ask him no more, I wouldn't get no more. But I was there everyday, beggin him, or as we said bugging him, but I was learning. I was a little bit dumb so that was why I was asking questions. I didn't want to stay dumb.

Now, we were rehearsing the group, Monte Carlo, we were playing, "Time Goes," "Passez Doubles" (PHONETIC). We had that type of band. And it was beautiful. Then we got a job to go to Atlantic City. (Inaudible) one of the clubs at Atlantic City. But it seems as though Charlie Johnson would usually go down there in the summer but we got the job. And oh, we had a beautiful time, man. I really got it together. And I turned 19, I got my mustache and I was really something special, then. Oh, yes, indeed. And I'd make…

But we were to go into a place on 59th (inaudible). It was a German place, it was a big restaurant, one of the high class restaurants, and we had to play in the afternoon. You had to play in the afternoon, we had to play the classics and airs and everything. Then at night we'd play for a lot of people, not too loud, (inaudible). But it was a beautiful job and the salary
